title: dedicated-gpu-pool-scheduling-autoscale-warmup-debug-breadcrumbs-20
content:
Summary:
Quick breadcrumbs for the warmup/autoscaler thrash incident on dedicated-gpu-pool-3 (02/27-02/28). Mostly notes-to-self + commands tried and hypotheses. Keep this as a scratchpad; will fold into INF-2314 timeline later.

Incident snapshot:
- Symptoms: repeated capacity churn (nodes added then removed within ~2-8 minutes), high variance in tail latency for small/medium requests, high number of warmup failures (containers failing readiness probe) during scale-up.
- Impact: ~15% elevated p95 for generation endpoints for ~3 hours. Affected customer traffic routed to fallback models for brief windows.

Initial checks (what I ran) — timeline + commands + short outputs:
1) Check autoscaler events (k8s cluster autoscaler + custom autoscaler logs)
- kubectl -n serving get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=dedicated-gpu-pool-3
  -> many events: PodScheduled, BackOff, FailedScheduling (insufficient nvidia.com/gpu) at times during churn.
- gcloud logging read "resource.labels.cluster_name=redwood-serving-prod AND jsonPayload.component=autoscaler" --limit 50
  -> discovered repeated scaleDown decisions immediately after scaleUp due to perceived low CPU usage in node pool metrics.

2) Readiness probe failures on warmup init container
- kubectl -n serving describe pod <pod-id>
  -> readiness probe failed: context deadline exceeded (post-warmup healthcheck hitting /healthz returned 500 in some cases). Logs show warmup script timed out waiting for model shards to map.
- /var/log/pods/<pod>/container-0.log snippet: "ERROR: kvcache init timeout after 45s; falling back to cold start"

3) Metrics & traces correlating scale decisions
- PromQL: sum(rate(kube_pod_container_status_ready[1m])) by (node) — observed flapping pods on newly created nodes.
- trace: warmup sequence shows step "load-shard" taking 30-90s depending on model, occasionally 300s+ when multiple warmups run concurrently on same GPU host.

Hypotheses so far:
- H1: Autoscaler scaleDown aggressiveness is calculated purely from CPU/memory metrics and ignores ongoing warmup progress (KV cache/model loading), so it thinks nodes are underutilized shortly after add and removes them before warmup completes => thrash.
- H2: Warmup script is single-threaded and contention for PCIe bandwidth or NVLink when multiple model loads happen concurrently on a new host leads to timeouts.
- H3: Readiness probe timeout values are too small for some heavy models (e.g., 13B quantized) — need to increase probe timeout or use staged readiness (service ready once model has minimal shards mapped).
- H4: Image/container startup variation (cold vs cached layers) sometimes causes longer startup; autoscaler interprets that as low utilization and scales down.

Experiments / changes tried and immediate outcomes:
A) Increased readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds from 10 -> 60 and timeoutSeconds from 5 -> 20 on canary pool (dedicated-gpu-pool-3-canary).
- Result: reduced early readiness failures for canary; warmup completed more often before scale decisions. Deployed to canary only.

B) Modified autoscaler policy to add a grace window: do not scaleDown nodes that were added < 10min. (patched config in autoscaler-config map and restarted controller)
- Result: eliminated immediate scaleDown after scaleUp in canary; overall p95 reduced for canary. Appears to address H1.

C) Throttled concurrent warmup operations per host: constrained warmup controller to max 2 concurrent model loads per GPU host (queueing additional warmups).
- Result: dramatic reduction in model load timeouts on canary nodes. Suggests contention (H2) is real.

D) Tried increasing kvcache init timeout to 120s in warmup script and switched to exponential backoff for retries.
- Result: fewer kvcache timeouts; however, some warmups still spiked >200s under high concurrency.

Observed unexpected behavior / gotchas:
- Autoscaler metrics: scale decisions are still influenced by node-level CPU metrics aggregated at 1m. Warmup CPU usage is low (loads are I/O bound), so the autoscaler often sees "low CPU" and scales down. Our change to grace window helped but feels like a band-aid.
- Billing/quota: keeping nodes around longer increases cost — need to balance with SLA.
- Some older GPU hosts (driver 525.x) showed slower model load than newer hosts (driver 530.x). Node labels not consistently used, so autoscaler might mix host types. Potential for scheduling new heavy-model pods onto slower hosts causing long warmups.

Debug snippets (copied outputs):
- autoscaler logs (trimmed): "ScaleDown: nodegroup=dedicated-pool-3 size=5 -> 3 reason=low_utilization observed=2m"
- warmup log: "[2026-02-27T22:13:11Z] load-shard: model=redwood-13b-q8b shard=0 start\n  [2026-02-27T22:15:03Z] load-shard: ERROR timeout after 120s"

Immediate next steps to stabilize (short term):
1) Roll autoscaler grace window change to prod pool for next 24h (monitor cost vs p95) — paired with alerting for prolonged unused nodes.
2) Roll readinessProbe increases across heavy-model deployments (careful with canary rollout).
3) Keep throttling concurrent warmups per host (configurable).

Longer-term TODOs / design items (tickets to create):
- INF-xxxx: Autoscaler awareness of "warmup in progress" signals (emit custom metric warmup_in_progress{node} and have scaleDown ignore nodes with warmup>0).
- INF-xxxx: Tag pools by GPU driver/host-class and prefer scheduling heavy-model warmups on faster hosts.
- INF-xxxx: Improve warmup to incremental readiness (shard-level readiness + traffic gating) so node is not considered "unused" while still warming.
- INF-xxxx: Revisit cost model for grace window vs commitment pricing (finance involvement).

Questions I still have / TODO for follow-ups:
- How many concurrent warmup jobs can a 8xA100 host sustain before PCIe/NVLink becomes bottleneck? Need benchmark.
- Is there an existing cluster-level annotation we can use to prefer newer-driver hosts? If not, add node labeling + scheduler affinity.
- How does Dedicated autoscaler interact with cloud provider node autoscaler? (we might be double-scaling).

Notes to self:
- Capture canary metrics dashboard queries (p95, number_of_warmups, kvcache_timeouts) and attach to INF-2314.
- Sync with Ravi tomorrow to decide whether to extend grace window permanently or implement warmup-aware metric first.

End of breadcrumbs. Will tidy and move into formal incident doc once we have final timeline and RCA.
